99.english_meaning: A new printing of a book or document that has already been published.

100.english_meaning: Impossible to divide or separate into smaller parts.
100.hindi_meaning: अविभाज्य (जिसे विभाजित न किया जा सके)
100.example: Dalton initially regarded the atom as the ultimate indivisible particle of matter.

100.english_meaning: Serving as a basic foundation or essential component.
100.example: Protons, neutrons, and electrons are the fundamental particles of an atom.

100.english_meaning: Fixed firmly into a surrounding mass.
100.example: Thomson proposed a model with electrons embedded into a sphere of positive electricity.

100.english_meaning: The process where particles are deflected or spread out after hitting a target.
100.example: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment proved the existence of the nucleus.

100.english_meaning: The state of being resistant to change or collapse.
100.example: The Rutherford model could not account for the stability of the atom.

100.english_meaning: Suggested or assumed the existence or truth of something as a basis for reasoning.
100.example: Bohr postulated that electrons move around the nucleus in circular orbits.

100.english_meaning: Plural of spectrum; bands of colors or energy levels produced by radiation.
100.example: The Bohr model successfully explained the spectra of the hydrogen atom.

100.english_meaning: The state of being unsure or the principle that certain pairs of physical properties cannot be known simultaneously.
100.example: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that position and velocity cannot be known exactly at the same time.

100.english_meaning: To assert the opposite of a statement or to be in conflict with.
100.example: The Bohr model contradicts the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

100.english_meaning: To take in or contain something as part of a whole.
100.example: The Schrödinger equation incorporates the concept of wave-particle duality.

100.english_meaning: The state of having two parts or aspects.
100.example: Wave-particle duality describes how matter exhibits both wave and particle properties.

100.english_meaning: Restricted to discrete, specific values rather than a continuous range.
100.example: Electrons in an atom occupy quantized energy states.

100.english_meaning: Relating to the angular measurement in a spherical coordinate system.
100.example: The azimuthal quantum number determines the shape of the orbital.

100.english_meaning: A result or effect of an action or condition.
100.example: Quantum numbers arise as a natural consequence of the Schrödinger equation.

100.english_meaning: Regions in an atom where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
100.hindi_meaning: कक्षक (इलेक्ट्रॉन पाए जाने की संभावना वाला क्षेत्र)
100.example: Subshells are composed of one or more orbitals.

101.english_meaning: Regions in an atom where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
101.hindi_meaning: परमाणु में वह क्षेत्र जहाँ इलेक्ट्रॉन पाए जाने की संभावना सबसे अधिक होती है।
101.example: Electrons are filled in orbitals in order of increasing energy.

101.english_meaning: The state of being manifold or various; in physics, related to the number of unpaired electrons.
101.hindi_meaning: बहुलता; क्वांटम यांत्रिकी में अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या से संबंधित।
101.example: Hund’s rule of maximum multiplicity governs how electrons fill subshells.

101.english_meaning: A subdivision of an electron shell, consisting of one or more orbitals.
101.hindi_meaning: इलेक्ट्रॉन कोश का एक उप-भाग, जिसमें एक या अधिक ऑर्बिटल होते हैं।
101.example: Each subshell must be singly occupied before pairing begins.

101.english_meaning: Plural of nucleus; the central part of an atom containing protons and neutrons.
101.hindi_meaning: नाभिक (बहुवचन); परमाणु का केंद्रीय भाग जिसमें प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं।
101.example: We need to determine the number of protons and neutrons in these nuclei.

101.english_meaning: The distance between successive crests of a wave.
101.hindi_meaning: तरंगदैर्घ्य; एक तरंग के दो क्रमिक शिखरों के बीच की दूरी।
101.example: The yellow light has a wavelength of 580 nm.

101.english_meaning: The number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit time.
101.hindi_meaning: आवृत्ति; प्रति इकाई समय में होने वाली घटनाओं की संख्या।
101.example: Calculate the frequency of the emitted light.

101.english_meaning: The number of wavelengths per unit distance.
101.hindi_meaning: तरंग संख्या; प्रति इकाई दूरी में तरंगदैर्घ्यों की संख्या।
101.example: The wavenumber is the reciprocal of the wavelength.

101.english_meaning: A particle representing a quantum of light or other electromagnetic radiation.
101.hindi_meaning: प्रकाश या विद्युत चुंबकीय विकिरण का एक कण (क्वांटम)।
101.example: Find the energy of each of the photons.

101.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from motion.
101.example: Calculate the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron.

101.english_meaning: Relating to the interrelation of electric currents and magnetic fields.
101.hindi_meaning: विद्युत चुंबकीय; विद्युत धाराओं और चुंबकीय क्षेत्रों के अंतर्संबंध से संबंधित।
101.example: Electromagnetic radiation is used to ionize the atom.

101.english_meaning: To convert an atom or molecule into an ion by removing or adding electrons.
101.hindi_meaning: आयनित करना; इलेक्ट्रॉन हटाकर या जोड़कर परमाणु को आयन में बदलना।
101.example: The radiation is sufficient to ionise the sodium atom.

101.english_meaning: Containing or using only one color or wavelength.
101.hindi_meaning: एकवर्णी; जिसमें केवल एक रंग या तरंगदैर्घ्य हो।
101.example: The bulb emits monochromatic yellow light.

101.english_meaning: Plural of quantum; the discrete, minimum amount of any physical entity involved in an interaction.
101.hindi_meaning: क्वांटा (बहुवचन); किसी भौतिक इकाई की न्यूनतम मात्रा।
101.example: Calculate the rate of emission of quanta per second.

101.english_meaning: The minimum level or intensity required for an effect to occur.
101.hindi_meaning: देहली; वह न्यूनतम स्तर जिस पर कोई प्रभाव उत्पन्न होता है।
101.example: Calculate the threshold frequency required for emission.

101.english_meaning: The process of changing from one state or level to another.
101.hindi_meaning: संक्रमण; एक अवस्था या स्तर से दूसरे में बदलने की प्रक्रिया।
101.example: The electron undergoes a transition from n=4 to n=2.

102.english_meaning: To convert an atom, molecule, or substance into an ion or ions, typically by removing one or more electrons.
102.hindi_meaning: किसी परमाणु या अणु से इलेक्ट्रॉन निकालकर उसे आयन में परिवर्तित करना।
102.example: Energy is required to ionise a hydrogen atom by removing its electron.

102.english_meaning: A thermodynamic quantity equivalent to the total heat content of a system.
102.hindi_meaning: ऊष्मागतिकी में किसी निकाय की कुल ऊष्मा मात्रा।
102.example: The ionization enthalpy measures the energy needed to remove an electron.

102.english_meaning: The production and discharge of something, especially radiation or light.
102.hindi_meaning: किसी चीज़ का उत्सर्जन, विशेषकर विकिरण या प्रकाश का।
102.example: The excited electron releases energy in the form of emission lines.

102.english_meaning: The number of wavelengths per unit distance, usually expressed in cm⁻¹.
102.hindi_meaning: प्रति इकाई दूरी में तरंगदैर्ध्य की संख्या।
102.example: Calculate the wavenumber for the longest wavelength transition.

102.english_meaning: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.
102.hindi_meaning: एक अवस्था से दूसरी अवस्था में परिवर्तन की प्रक्रिया।
102.example: The electron undergoes a transition from a higher orbit to a lower one.

102.english_meaning: Having the same number of electrons or a similar electronic structure.
102.hindi_meaning: समान संख्या में इलेक्ट्रॉन रखने वाले परमाणु या आयन।
102.example: Na+ and Mg2+ are isoelectronic species as they have the same number of electrons.

102.english_meaning: The arrangement of electrons in the orbitals of an atom or molecule.
102.hindi_meaning: परमाणु या अणु के कक्षकों में इलेक्ट्रॉनों की व्यवस्था।
102.example: Write the electronic configuration of the following ions.

102.english_meaning: A region in an atom where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
102.hindi_meaning: परमाणु का वह क्षेत्र जहाँ इलेक्ट्रॉन पाए जाने की संभावना सबसे अधिक होती है (कक्षक)।
102.example: The electron is located in one of the 3d orbitals.

102.english_meaning: A discrete quantity of energy proportional in magnitude to the frequency of the radiation it represents.
102.example: Quantum numbers describe the properties of electrons in an atom.

102.english_meaning: To arrive at a fact or a conclusion by reasoning; to draw as a logical conclusion.
102.hindi_meaning: तर्क द्वारा किसी निष्कर्ष पर पहुँचना या अनुमान लगाना।
102.example: Deduce the number of protons from the given information.

102.english_meaning: The speed of something in a given direction.
102.hindi_meaning: किसी निश्चित दिशा में वस्तु की गति (वेग)।
102.example: The electron is moving with a velocity of 2.05 × 10⁷ m/s.

102.english_meaning: In physics, an atom or electron that has absorbed energy and moved to a higher energy state.
102.hindi_meaning: उच्च ऊर्जा स्तर पर पहुँचा हुआ परमाणु या इलेक्ट्रॉन (उत्तेजित अवस्था)।

102.english_meaning: The lowest energy state of an atom or other quantum system.
102.hindi_meaning: परमाणु की न्यूनतम ऊर्जा वाली अवस्था (मूल अवस्था)।
102.example: The electron returns to the ground state after emitting light.

102.english_meaning: In chemistry, a distinct chemical entity such as an atom, molecule, or ion.
102.hindi_meaning: रसायन विज्ञान में एक विशिष्ट रासायनिक इकाई जैसे परमाणु, अणु या आयन।
102.example: Identify which of the following are isoelectronic species.

102.english_meaning: A system of characters, symbols, or abbreviated expressions used in an art or science.
102.hindi_meaning: विज्ञान में प्रयुक्त संकेतों या प्रतीकों की प्रणाली।
102.example: Use s, p, d notations to describe the orbital.

103.english_meaning: The minimum amount of any physical entity involved in an interaction.
103.hindi_meaning: किसी भौतिक राशि की न्यूनतम मात्रा या ऊर्जा का पैकेट।
103.example: The energy of a photon is a quantum of electromagnetic radiation.

103.english_meaning: The enclosing boundary of a curved geometric figure, especially a circle.
103.hindi_meaning: किसी वृत्त या गोलाकार आकृति की परिधि।

103.english_meaning: Necessary to make a whole complete; in mathematics, relating to integers.

103.english_meaning: The distance between successive crests of a wave.
103.hindi_meaning: तरंगदैर्ध्य (दो क्रमागत तरंगों के बीच की दूरी)।
103.example: The wavelength of the radiation determines its frequency.

103.english_meaning: The process of changing from one state or condition to another.
103.hindi_meaning: एक अवस्था से दूसरी अवस्था में परिवर्तन।
103.example: The electron transition results in the emission of light.

103.english_meaning: The process by which an atom or a molecule acquires a negative or positive charge.
103.hindi_meaning: आयनीकरण (परमाणु से इलेक्ट्रॉन निकलने की प्रक्रिया)।
103.example: Ionization energy is required to remove an electron from the atom.

103.english_meaning: To attack or hit something continuously with particles or radiation.
103.hindi_meaning: लगातार प्रहार करना या बमबारी करना।

103.english_meaning: Lacking in movement, action, or change; relating to stationary electric charges.

103.english_meaning: The emission of energy as electromagnetic waves or as moving subatomic particles.
103.hindi_meaning: विकिरण (ऊर्जा का तरंगों के रूप में निकलना)।
103.example: X-rays are a form of high-energy radiation.

103.english_meaning: The rate at which something occurs or is repeated over a particular period of time.
103.hindi_meaning: आवृत्ति (प्रति सेकंड होने वाली दोलनों की संख्या)।
103.example: The frequency of the light wave is very high.

103.english_meaning: A particle representing a quantum of light or other electromagnetic radiation.
103.hindi_meaning: प्रकाश का कण (प्रकाश की ऊर्जा का पैकेट)।
103.example: The laser emits a large number of photons.

103.english_meaning: The production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.
103.hindi_meaning: उत्सर्जन (किसी पदार्थ या ऊर्जा का बाहर निकलना)।
103.example: Neon gas shows strong emission at specific wavelengths.

103.english_meaning: The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus.
103.hindi_meaning: द्रव्यमान संख्या (प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन की कुल संख्या)।

103.english_meaning: A band of colors or range of frequencies produced by separation of components of light.

103.example: The hydrogen spectrum shows distinct lines of light.

103.english_meaning: Metal hammered or rolled into a very thin flexible sheet.
103.example: Rutherford used a thin gold foil in his experiment.

104.english_meaning: Relating to the scientific study of stars, planets, and other objects in space.
104.example: Astronomical observations help us understand the composition of distant stars.

104.english_meaning: A particle representing a quantum of light or other electromagnetic radiation.
104.example: The detector counts every single photon emitted by the source.

104.english_meaning: A state of an atom or molecule having more energy than its ground state.
104.example: Electrons in the excited state are unstable and eventually return to a lower energy level.

104.english_meaning: A pair of closely spaced spectral lines in an emission or absorption spectrum.
104.example: The doublet absorption transition was clearly visible in the experimental data.

104.english_meaning: The minimum energy required to remove an electron from the surface of a metal.
104.hindi_meaning: कार्य फलन (धातु की सतह से इलेक्ट्रॉन निकालने के लिए आवश्यक न्यूनतम ऊर्जा)
104.example: Caesium has a low work function, making it ideal for photoelectric experiments.

104.english_meaning: The minimum level or intensity required for a physical effect to occur.
104.example: The radiation must exceed the threshold frequency to eject a photoelectron.

104.english_meaning: Exposed to radiation, such as light or X-rays.
104.example: The metal surface was irradiated with ultraviolet light to observe the effect.

104.english_meaning: An electron emitted from a material as a result of the photoelectric effect.
104.example: The kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectron depends on the frequency of the incident light.

104.english_meaning: The production and discharge of something, especially radiation or light.
104.example: The emission spectrum of hydrogen reveals specific energy transitions.

104.english_meaning: A band of colors or frequencies produced by separation of the components of light.
104.example: The transition falls within the infrared region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

104.english_meaning: The process by which a beam of light or other system of waves is spread out as a result of passing through a narrow aperture.
104.example: Electron diffraction provides evidence for the wave-like nature of matter.

104.english_meaning: The state of being unsure or the range within which a measurement may vary.
104.example: Heisenberg's principle describes the inherent uncertainty in measuring position and momentum.

104.english_meaning: The quantity of motion of a moving body, measured as a product of its mass and velocity.
104.example: The uncertainty in the electron's momentum increases as its position is more precisely defined.

104.english_meaning: Values that describe the energy levels, shape, and orientation of orbitals in an atom.
104.example: Quantum numbers are used to define the state of an electron in an atom.

104.english_meaning: The difference in electric potential between two points, measured in volts.
104.example: A potential difference of 1000 V was applied to accelerate the proton.

105.english_meaning: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.
105.example: The structure of the atom explains how electrons are arranged around the nucleus.

105.english_meaning: A mathematical function describing the location and wave-like behavior of an electron in an atom.
105.example: Electrons are found in specific regions called orbitals.

105.english_meaning: The net positive charge experienced by an electron in a multi-electron atom.
105.example: The effective nuclear charge determines how strongly an electron is attracted to the nucleus.

105.english_meaning: Not forming a pair; existing singly.
105.example: The atom has several unpaired electrons in its outer shell.

105.english_meaning: A subdivision of electron shells separated by electron orbitals.
105.example: The n=4 energy level contains multiple subshells.

105.english_meaning: The positively charged central core of an atom, consisting of protons and neutrons.
105.example: The nucleus contains almost all of the mass of the atom.
There are four subshells associated with the fourth energy level.
Please indicate the number of electrons in the given orbital.

105.english_meaning: To have as belonging to one; own.
105.example: The bromine atom possesses thirty-five electrons in total.

105.english_meaning: Values that describe the energy levels and characteristics of electrons in an atom.
105.example: The values of n, l, ml, and ms are known as quantum numbers.

105.english_meaning: A stable subatomic particle with a negative charge.
105.example: Each electron occupies a specific orbital based on its energy.

105.english_meaning: The fixed amount of energy that an electron in an atom may have.
105.example: Electrons move to a higher energy level when they absorb energy.

105.english_meaning: A set of two things used together or regarded as a unit.
105.example: Compare the effective nuclear charge of the given pair of orbitals.

105.english_meaning: To undergo or be affected by a force or condition.
105.example: Inner electrons experience a stronger pull from the nucleus.

105.english_meaning: The numerical amount denoted by an algebraic term.
105.example: The ms value for these electrons is negative one-half.

106.english_meaning: Happening or appearing at regular intervals.
106.hindi_meaning: आवर्ती (जो एक निश्चित अंतराल पर घटित हो)
106.example: The periodic nature of the seasons helps farmers plan their crops.

106.english_meaning: Brief, clearly expressed, and to the point.
106.example: The teacher gave a succinct explanation of the complex chemical theory.

106.english_meaning: To separate things that have become joined or confused.
106.example: Science helps us disentangle the mysteries of the natural world.

106.english_meaning: The arrangement of parts or elements in a particular form or figure.
106.example: The electronic configuration of an atom determines its chemical behavior.

106.english_meaning: A system of names for things, especially in a scientific field.
106.example: IUPAC nomenclature provides a standard way to name chemical elements.

106.english_meaning: The tendency of a substance to undergo chemical reaction.
106.example: The reactivity of alkali metals increases as you move down the group.

106.english_meaning: To show or find a relationship or connection between two things.
106.example: We can correlate the atomic size with the ionization enthalpy of the element.

106.english_meaning: The energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom.
106.example: Ionization enthalpy is a key property in understanding periodic trends.

106.english_meaning: The combining power of an element, especially as measured by the number of hydrogen atoms it can displace or combine with.
106.example: The valence of oxygen is two, which explains why it forms water with two hydrogen atoms.

106.english_meaning: To produce a substance by chemical or physical combination.
106.example: Scientists continue to synthesise new heavy elements in the laboratory.
There are innumerable compounds formed by the combination of different elements.

106.english_meaning: To make something logical and consistent.
106.example: The periodic table helps to rationalize the vast amount of chemical data.

106.english_meaning: Forming a necessary base or core; of central importance.
106.example: Elements are the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

106.english_meaning: Things with distinct and independent existence.
106.example: Chemical elements are distinct entities with unique properties.

106.english_meaning: A measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons.
106.example: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all the elements.

107.english_meaning: The origin or mode of formation of something.
107.example: The genesis of the periodic table lies in the early observations of chemical properties.

107.english_meaning: The action or process of classifying something according to shared qualities or characteristics.
107.example: The classification of elements helps scientists understand their behavior systematically.

107.english_meaning: To arrange according to an organized system.
107.example: Scientists spent years systematising the data collected from various experiments.

107.english_meaning: A group or set of three connected people or things.
107.example: Dobereiner identified groups of three elements known as Triads.

107.english_meaning: The fact of occurring again at intervals.
107.example: The periodic recurrence of properties is the fundamental basis of the modern periodic table.

107.english_meaning: To put forward an idea or theory for consideration by others.
107.example: John Newlands profounded the Law of Octaves in 1865.

107.english_meaning: A series of eight notes occupying the interval between two notes.
107.example: Newlands compared the repetition of chemical properties to musical octaves.

107.english_meaning: An expert in the science that deals with the earth's physical structure and substance.
107.example: A French geologist attempted to classify elements using a cylindrical table.

107.english_meaning: Having the shape of a cylinder.
107.example: He arranged the elements on a cylindrical surface to show their periodic trends.

107.english_meaning: A remarkable concurrence of events or circumstances without apparent causal connection.
107.example: Initially, the Law of Triads was dismissed by many as a mere coincidence.

107.english_meaning: Free from outside control; not depending on another's authority.
107.example: Mendeleev and Meyer worked independently to develop the Periodic Law.

107.english_meaning: A space between two things; a period of time between two events.
107.example: Properties of elements repeat at regular intervals in the periodic table.

107.english_meaning: The mass of an atom of a chemical element expressed in atomic mass units.
107.example: Early classification systems were based on the increasing order of atomic weight.

107.english_meaning: Marked or traced on a chart or graph.
107.example: Lothar Meyer plotted atomic volume against atomic weight on a graph.

107.english_meaning: A result or effect of an action or condition.
107.example: The periodic table is one of the consequences of centuries of scientific observation.

108.english_meaning: The quality or character of being periodic; the tendency to recur at intervals.
108.hindi_meaning: आवर्तता (निश्चित अंतराल पर दोहराए जाने का गुण)
108.example: Mendeleev fully recognized the significance of periodicity in the arrangement of elements.

108.english_meaning: Based on observation or experience rather than theory or pure logic.
108.hindi_meaning: अनुभवजन्य (जो प्रयोगों या प्रेक्षणों पर आधारित हो)
108.example: Mendeleev relied on the empirical formulas of compounds to classify elements.

108.english_meaning: The average mass of atoms of an element, measured in atomic mass units.
108.example: Elements were arranged in order of their increasing atomic weights.

108.english_meaning: The action or process of classifying something according to shared qualities or characteristics.
108.example: Mendeleev's system of classification was more elaborate than his predecessors'.

108.english_meaning: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.
108.example: The boldness of Mendeleev’s quantitative predictions made his table famous.

108.english_meaning: Involving many carefully arranged parts or details; detailed and complicated.
